prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_F:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2005 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core message: Britain has great potential but is heading in the wrong direction under Labour. The Conservatives promise action over talk, rewarding hard work, restoring accountability, devolving power, and focusing on practical priorities: cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes.

Economy and tax:
- Cut waste and borrowing to fund tax cuts: save £12bn/year by 2007–08 (civil service freeze, 235,000 fewer bureaucratic posts, scrap/merge 168 bodies); use £8bn to reduce borrowing and £4bn for tax cuts.
- Lower, simpler taxes to promote work and enterprise; keep minimum wage and planned rises.
- Halve council tax bills (up to £500) for households where all residents are over 65, funded centrally.
- Pensions: restore earnings link for the basic state pension; keep Winter Fuel Payment, over-75 TV licences, and 2005 council tax payment. Create Lifetime Savings Accounts; strengthen workplace pensions (opt-out schemes); use unclaimed financial assets to protect failed scheme members.
- Stability: keep Bank of England independence; no to the Euro. Deregulation via regulatory budgets, sunset reviews, end EU “gold-plating”; restore UK opt-out from EU Social Chapter.

Education and families:
- Flexible childcare: more flexible maternity pay; up to £50/week per under-5 via Working Tax Credit for all qualifying working families, usable for formal or informal care; support workplace nurseries and after-school clubs.
- Restore discipline: give heads/governors full control over admissions/expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; protect teachers from malicious allegations; slash paperwork; funding to follow the pupil.
- Raise standards: scrap grade-inflation targets; publish marks alongside grades; allow international qualifications; slim and depoliticise the National Curriculum; 300,000 vocational grants for 14–16s; more sport (two hours after-school) and ban junk food in schools.
- Higher/further education: scrap university tuition fees; abolish the admissions regulator; build endowments; simplify FE funding and empower “super colleges.”

NHS and social care:
- Increase NHS funding by £34bn over the Parliament; shift power to professionals; abolish Strategic Health Authorities, cut PCTs and quangos; end central targets; funding to follow patients; more single rooms and infection control; restore matrons with power to close wards; protect community hospitals.
- End waiting lists as we know them; offer NHS contribution (half NHS cost) for self-pay operations to cut queues.
- Reform dentistry (low monthly payment option); more support for carers; partnership scheme so no one must sell their home for long-term care.
- Health checks for long-stay non-EU migrants; STI public health campaign.

Crime and security:
- 5,000 extra police officers each year; slash paperwork; elected police commissioners; genuine neighbourhood policing.
- 20,000 extra prison places; end early release; honesty in sentencing.
- Drugs: 25,000 residential rehab places; hard-drug users: treatment or court; reclassify cannabis to Class B.
- Appoint a Homeland Security Minister; robust counter-terror measures.

Immigration and borders:
- Controlled immigration with popular consent: 24/7 port surveillance, restored embarkation controls, create a British Border Control Police.
- Australian-style points system prioritising needed skills.
- Asylum: repatriate powers from the EU; replace the 1951 Geneva framework with modern agreements; process claims outside the UK; fixed annual refugee quota via UNHCR; overall annual immigration limit set by Parliament.

Constitution, communities, and environment:
- Accountability: Timetable for Action; ministers who fail will go. Abolish regional assemblies; strengthen Parliament and select committees; cut MPs by 20%; English votes for English laws.
- Devolution: back the Union; Welsh referendum on Assembly powers; stricter standards for NI executive participation.
- Localism: devolve planning/housing/transport/fire to councils; tougher action on illegal traveller camps; devolve arts and Lottery decisions.
- Housing: extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership.
- Transport: end “war on motorists”; modernise roads; review all speed cameras; longer rail franchises.
- Environment: protect Green Belt, prioritise brownfield; phase out HFCs; lower VED for low-emission cars; boost home energy efficiency; expand renewables and energy security; more recycling.
- Rural/agriculture: honest food labelling; require Little Red Tractor in public procurement; push CAP reform; strengthen animal welfare; free vote to overturn hunting ban.

Foreign policy and defence:
- Spend £2.7bn more on the military front line by 2007–08; preserve regiments and warships; NATO at the core; support service families.
- Iraq: stay to rebuild and support democracy; pursue Middle East peace (secure Israel and viable Palestinian state).
- Europe: oppose EU Constitution (referendum within six months); no Euro; restore Social Chapter opt-out; repatriate fisheries control; back enlargement including Turkey.
- Aid: meet 0.7% of GNI by 2013; increase UK control of aid; champion open markets, rule of law and property rights.

First-month actions: begin recruiting 5,000 extra police per year; restore matrons; first Budget to cut waste and lower taxes; empower heads to expel; start 24/7 port surveillance; set date for EU Constitution referendum (campaign for No).

TEXT_C:
Green Party Manifesto 2005 — Summary (under 500 words)

Vision: Build a sustainable society grounded in social, economic and environmental justice. Reverse privatisation of public services, place peace and human rights at the core of foreign policy, and act decisively on climate change.

Economy
- Tackle inequality with progressive taxation: 50% on income over £50k; 60% over £100k. More corporation tax bands (40% for profits >£1.5m). Increase taxes on unearned wealth; recipient-based, progressive inheritance tax.
- Abolish National Insurance; tax all income uniformly. Pilot Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
- Replace VAT with revenue-neutral eco-taxes on resource use, pollution and waste; include aviation fuel and plastic bags.
- Promote economic localisation: community banks, credit unions, local currencies; support small businesses and co-ops; oppose joining the euro; reform WTO.
- Create green jobs via renewables, low-carbon transport, zero-waste. Strengthen workers’ rights; reduce working hours. Measure well-being beyond GDP (ISEW/MDP).

Energy and Climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence: CO2 cuts of 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020, 85% by 2030; develop full carbon trading.
- Replace domestic VAT and Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax; protect low-income users via tariff reform.
- Target 40% renewable energy by 2020; invest in solar, wind (on/offshore), wave, and biogas; two million small-scale wind systems and two million m² solar by 2010.
- Cut demand: Warmer Homes Act (30% domestic reduction in 10 years); Smart Energy Councils (45% emission cut by 2020).
- Close nuclear as stations reach end-of-life; shift R&D subsidies to renewables; Cabinet post for climate policy.

Welfare
- Phase in a universal Citizen’s Income replacing most means-tested benefits; retain disability/incapacity benefits; integrate housing benefit later.
- Citizen’s Pension: universal, earnings-linked, replaces Pension Credit; initial level at Pension Credit Guarantee.
- Increase child support; simplify systems; expand Sure Start; end Working Time Directive opt-out; move toward 35-hour week.
- Housing: let councils build with sales receipts; support self-build co-ops; drive insulation/efficiency; reform land via LVT.

Health and Education
- Restore NHS principles; end PPPs/foundation hospitals; oppose GATS in healthcare. Abolish prescription charges; free eye tests and dental; support holistic treatments.
- Fund NHS to at least 9% of GNP (~£90bn); consider hypothecated NHS Tax; prioritise prevention and mental health.
- Boost education funding, expand Children’s Centres; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants (align with Citizen’s Income); abolish SATs; introduce individual learning plans.

Transport
- Shift to walking, cycling, public transport, rail freight; cut road traffic 10% by 2010; redirect £30bn from roads to public transport; re-regulate buses.
- Return rail and tube to public ownership; expand rail lines, stations, freight, and light rail.
- Price true motoring costs: extend congestion/road pricing; raise fuel duty; abolish tax disc; size/pollution-based freight duty; invest in cleaner vehicle R&D.
- Curb aviation: resist airport expansion; ban night flights; EU-wide aviation fuel tax; domestic emissions tax; raise APD; shift short-haul to rail.

Environment, Food, Farming, Animal Welfare
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration; 60% domestic recycling by 2010; Zero Waste Agency; eco-taxes on harmful inputs; stronger chemicals regulation.
- Precautionary principle on GM, xenotransplantation, nanotech; oppose TRIPS patents on natural resources.
- End live exports; ban battery eggs (incl. enriched); tougher broiler standards; ban fur; end vivisection.
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic by 2012; support local markets. Replace CAP/CFP with support for organics, biodiversity, sustainable incomes. Ban GM food; strengthen supermarket Code with legal watchdog; review OFT.

Crime and Justice
- Prevent crime via urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, visible staff; treat drugs as health issue; oppose ID cards.
- More community policing, local stations, neighbourhood committees; independent complaints system.
- Tough gun controls: prohibit dangerous categories; regulate deactivated guns; single licensing with competence/stability checks; advisory committee.
- Expand restorative justice; strengthen response to hate crimes, violence against women; EU-wide disability rights.

Democracy
- Oppose ID cards. Revive local government with powers (incl. LVT), PR elections, recall (40%) and local referenda (20%).
- PR for Westminster and local councils; elected Lords by PR; regional government by local choice; more powers for Scotland/Wales.
- Written constitution; disestablish Church of England; remove monarchy’s formal roles. Campaign No to proposed EU constitution.

International
- Ethical foreign policy: withdraw from Iraq, support UN peacekeeping; cut defence to EU average; end arms export subsidies; arms trade treaty; decommission nuclear weapons.
- Aid at least 1% GNI by 2010; cancel debts of 52 poorest; support Tobin tax; equitable carbon trading.
- Reform UN (no permanent Security Council seats, majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank.
- Replace/overhaul WTO with General Agreement on Sustainable Trade favouring localisation and standards.
- Asylum: uphold rights, allow work/benefits, resource decisions, independent appeals; ratify UN migrant workers convention; honour Refugee Convention; review restrictive UK laws.

Judge whether TEXT_F or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",

}
